mi.title: One imagined left-hand trial
mi.note: C3 is over the left motor cortex, C4 over the right. The epoch is already band-passed 8–32 Hz by the benchmark, which is why the ~10 Hz mu rhythm is so visible.

p300.title: Target vs standard flashes
p300.source: BNCI 2014-008, subject 1, averaged at Pz (700 target, 3,500 standard flashes)
p300.note: The target average has a positive deflection around 400 ms — the P300. It is small in a single trial, which is why the benchmark uses a decoder rather than a peak-picker.

ssvep.title: The flicker shows up in the spectrum
ssvep.source: Nakanishi 2015, subject 1, 15 trials of the 13.75 Hz target, electrode Oz
ssvep.note: The peak sits exactly at the flicker frequency; the smaller peak near 27.5 Hz is its second harmonic. The CCA decoder looks for this pattern, not at the raw wiggle.

motor_auc.title: One electrode, left vs right fist
motor_auc.source: Wu 2020, 6 subjects, beta band 13–30 Hz, 5-fold CV
motor_auc.note: The best scalp electrode clears chance; no single ear electrode does. This is a per-electrode view of the same site-vs-count question the montage experiment asks.

sleep.title: One night, scored every 30 seconds
sleep.note: The model sees one 30-second window at a time. The visual is the sequence it is trying to recover. Stage codes come from the dataset's own events.json.

stew.title: Rest vs multitasking, one electrode
stew.source: STEW, subject 01, electrode AF3, whole 150 s recordings
stew.note: The multitasking recording carries more power above ~13 Hz (muscle and movement) and a weaker alpha peak. The decoder reads band power, so these differences are its input â€” and they are also why rest-vs-task is easier than it looks.

earsaad.title: Decoding a followed voice, 60 s windows
earsaad.note: Grey bars are scalp references trimmed to the same channel count as the ear arrays, so the scalp-vs-ear gap is not a channel-count gap. Whiskers are Â±1 s.d. across subjects.

faced.title: Positive vs negative valence, by placement
faced.source: FACED, 123 participants, participant-disjoint CV, 4 s windows
faced.note: Every bar is close to chance, and that is the finding: the effect is real but small. The best four electrodes are posterior, not the frontal sites a glasses frame would use.
